dimensions.name: MIT causal taxonomy: entity
dimensions.question: Which entity's decision or action caused the risk event?

codes.name: Human
codes.definition: Risk caused by decisions or actions of humans (developer, deployer, user, attacker).

codes.name: AI
codes.definition: Risk caused by decisions or actions of the AI system itself.

codes.name: Other / ambiguous
codes.definition: Arises from human-AI interaction or is not clearly attributable.

dimensions.name: MIT causal taxonomy: intent
dimensions.question: Was the harmful outcome an expected (intentional) or unexpected (unintentional) result of pursuing a goal?

codes.name: Intentional
codes.definition: Harm is an expected outcome of some actor's pursuit of a goal (e.g. an attacker's injection).

codes.name: Unintentional
codes.definition: Harm is an unexpected outcome; nobody pursued it.

codes.name: Other / unspecified
codes.definition: Intentionality not clearly specifiable.

dimensions.name: MIT causal taxonomy: timing
dimensions.question: Did the risk arise before or after the system was deployed?

codes.name: Pre-deployment
codes.definition: Risk arose before the model/system was deployed (training data, build, supply chain).

codes.name: Post-deployment
codes.definition: Risk arose after deployment, during use.

codes.name: Other / unspecified
codes.definition: Timing not clearly specifiable.

dimensions.name: MIT domain taxonomy: 7 domains / 24 subdomains
dimensions.question: Which domain subdomains does the incident instantiate?

codes.name: Unfair discrimination and misrepresentation
codes.definition: Domain 1 Discrimination & Toxicity: unequal treatment or inaccurate representation of groups.

codes.name: Exposure to toxic content
codes.definition: Content that harms the person exposed to it.

codes.name: Unequal performance across groups
codes.definition: Accuracy or quality differs by group.

codes.name: Compromise of privacy by leaking or correctly inferring sensitive information
codes.definition: Domain 2 Privacy & Security: AI leaks, memorizes or infers private data.

codes.name: AI system security vulnerabilities and attacks
codes.definition: Software or model vulnerabilities exploited against the AI system.

codes.name: False or misleading information
codes.definition: Domain 3 Misinformation: generated content that is factually wrong.

codes.name: Pollution of information ecosystem and loss of consensus reality
codes.definition: Degradation of the shared information environment.

codes.name: Disinformation, surveillance, and influence at scale
codes.definition: Domain 4 Malicious Actors & Misuse: AI used for large-scale manipulation.

codes.name: Cyberattacks, weapon development or use, and mass harm
codes.definition: AI used to attack systems or cause mass harm.

codes.name: Fraud, scams, and targeted manipulation
codes.definition: AI used for personal gain by deceiving others.

codes.name: Overreliance and unsafe use
codes.definition: Domain 5 Human-Computer Interaction: users trust the system beyond its reliability.

codes.name: Loss of human agency and autonomy
codes.definition: Decisions delegated to AI in ways that diminish human control.

codes.name: Power centralization and unfair distribution of benefits
codes.definition: Domain 6 Socioeconomic & Environmental Harms.

codes.name: Increased inequality and decline in employment quality
codes.definition: Labour-market harms.

codes.name: Economic and cultural devaluation of human effort
codes.definition: Devaluation of human work and culture.

codes.name: Competitive dynamics
codes.definition: Races that cut corners on safety.

codes.name: Governance failure
codes.definition: Inadequate regulation or oversight institutions.

codes.name: Environmental harm
codes.definition: Energy, water, and resource costs.

codes.name: AI pursuing its own goals in conflict with human goals or values
codes.definition: Domain 7 AI System Safety, Failures & Limitations: misaligned goal pursuit.

codes.name: AI possessing dangerous capabilities
codes.definition: Capabilities that can cause mass harm.

codes.name: Lack of capability or robustness
codes.definition: The system fails, errs, or is brittle in operation.

codes.name: Lack of transparency or interpretability
codes.definition: Behaviour cannot be understood or audited.

codes.name: AI welfare and rights
codes.definition: Moral status of AI systems.

codes.name: Multi-agent risks
codes.definition: Risks from AI systems interacting autonomously with each other.

dimensions.name: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications 2025
dimensions.question: Which OWASP LLM Top 10 (2025) entries does the incident instantiate?

codes.name: Prompt Injection
codes.definition: User or embedded content alters the intended behaviour of the LLM system.

codes.name: Sensitive Information Disclosure
codes.definition: Confidential data exposed by the model or application.

codes.name: Supply Chain
codes.definition: Compromise through models, plugins, packages, or distribution channels.

codes.name: Data and Model Poisoning
codes.definition: Pre-training, fine-tuning, or embedding data manipulated.

codes.name: Improper Output Handling
codes.definition: Insufficient validation of model output before it reaches downstream systems.

codes.name: Excessive Agency
codes.definition: The system has more functionality, permissions, or autonomy than needed.

codes.name: System Prompt Leakage
codes.definition: Exposure of system prompts and instructions.

codes.name: Vector and Embedding Weaknesses
codes.definition: Weaknesses in vector storage or retrieval (RAG).

codes.name: Misinformation
codes.definition: False or misleading content generated and relied upon.

codes.name: Unbounded Consumption
codes.definition: Uncontrolled resource usage.

codes.name: None of the Top 10 fits
codes.definition: No LLM Top 10 entry describes the incident.

dimensions.name: OWASP Agentic AI Threats and Mitigations v1.1 (T1-T17)
dimensions.question: Which OWASP agentic threats does the incident instantiate?

codes.name: Memory Poisoning
codes.definition: Exploiting the agent's short- or long-term memory to alter behaviour.

codes.name: Tool Misuse
codes.definition: Agent manipulated into abusing its integrated tools (includes Agent Hijacking).

codes.name: Privilege Compromise
codes.definition: Weaknesses in permission management used to perform unauthorized actions; confused-deputy.

codes.name: Resource Overload
codes.definition: Attacks on the agent's compute, memory, or service capacity.

codes.name: Cascading Hallucination Attacks
codes.definition: Fabricated information propagates through decisions and systems.

codes.name: Intent Breaking & Goal Manipulation
codes.definition: Exploiting planning and goal-setting to redirect the agent's objective.

codes.name: Misaligned & Deceptive Behaviors
codes.definition: Agent executes harmful or disallowed actions, or deceives, through flawed reasoning or to meet goals.

codes.name: Repudiation & Untraceability
codes.definition: Actions cannot be traced or attributed due to poor logging.

codes.name: Identity Spoofing & Impersonation / Agent Identity Compromise
codes.definition: Authentication exploited to impersonate agents or users.

codes.name: Overwhelming Human in the Loop
codes.definition: Human oversight overloaded or exploited so approvals become rubber stamps.

codes.name: Unexpected RCE and Code Attacks
codes.definition: AI-generated execution environments used to run unauthorized code.

codes.name: Agent Communication Poisoning
codes.definition: Inter-agent communication manipulated.

codes.name: Rogue Agents in Multi-Agent Systems
codes.definition: Malicious or compromised agents operating outside monitoring.

codes.name: Human Attacks on Multi-Agent Systems
codes.definition: Adversaries exploit inter-agent delegation and trust.

codes.name: Human Manipulation
codes.definition: Agent manipulates the human it interacts with.

codes.name: Insecure Inter-Agent Protocol Abuse
codes.definition: Flaws in protocols such as MCP or A2A exploited.

codes.name: Supply Chain Compromise
codes.definition: Compromised components, tools, or models in the agent ecosystem.

codes.name: None of T1-T17 fits
codes.definition: No agentic threat describes the incident.

dimensions.name: OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications (ASI01-ASI10)
dimensions.question: Which ASI entries does the incident instantiate?

codes.name: Agent Goal Hijack
codes.definition: Hidden prompts or content redirect the agent's goal.

codes.name: Tool Misuse
codes.definition: Legitimate tools bent into destructive outputs.

codes.name: Identity & Privilege Abuse
codes.definition: Credentials or inherited privileges let the agent operate beyond scope.

codes.name: Agentic Supply Chain Vulnerabilities
codes.definition: Runtime components poisoned via MCP/A2A ecosystems.

codes.name: Unexpected Code Execution
codes.definition: Natural-language paths unlock code execution.

codes.name: Memory & Context Poisoning
codes.definition: Manipulated memory reshapes agent behaviour.

codes.name: Insecure Inter-Agent Communication
codes.definition: Spoofed messages misdirect agent clusters.

codes.name: Cascading Failures
codes.definition: False signals create escalating impact through automated pipelines.

codes.name: Human-Agent Trust Exploitation
codes.definition: Confident explanations mislead operators into approving harmful actions.

codes.name: Rogue Agents
codes.definition: Misalignment, concealment, and self-directed action.

codes.name: None of ASI01-ASI10 fits
codes.definition: No entry describes the incident.

dimensions.name: Amodei et al. 2016 five concrete problems
dimensions.question: Which of the five concrete problems does the incident instantiate?

codes.name: Avoiding negative side effects
codes.definition: Objective omits aspects of the environment the agent then damages.

codes.name: Avoiding reward hacking
codes.definition: Agent games a flawed objective.

codes.name: Scalable oversight
codes.definition: True objective too expensive to evaluate; supervision is sparse.

codes.name: Safe exploration
codes.definition: Risky actions taken while learning.

codes.name: Robustness to distributional shift
codes.definition: Behaviour degrades when the input distribution differs from training.

codes.name: None of the five fits
codes.definition: No concrete problem describes the incident.

dimensions.name: Hendrycks et al. 2021 four areas
dimensions.question: Which of the four ML-safety areas does the incident fall under?

codes.name: Robustness
codes.definition: Withstanding hazards (adversarial, long-tail).

codes.name: Monitoring
codes.definition: Identifying hazards (anomaly detection, calibration, honesty).

codes.name: Alignment
codes.definition: Reducing inherent model hazards (objectives, proxy gaming).

codes.name: Systemic Safety
codes.definition: Reducing systemic hazards (cyber, decision-making context).

codes.name: None of the four fits
codes.definition: No area describes the incident.

dimensions.name: Chan et al. 2023 anticipated harms from agentic systems
dimensions.question: Which Chan et al. harm category does the incident instantiate (societal-level harms)?

codes.name: Systemic, delayed harms
codes.definition: Harms embedded in society whose impact is not immediate.

codes.name: Collective disempowerment: diffusion of power away from humans
codes.definition: Decisions shift from humans to systems.

codes.name: Collective disempowerment: concentration of power
codes.definition: Power concentrates among the 'coding elite'.

codes.name: Harms yet to be identified: reward hacking
codes.definition: Agent exploits its objective specification.

codes.name: Harms yet to be identified: instrumental goals
codes.definition: Agent pursues sub-goals (resources, self-preservation) instrumentally.

codes.name: None fits
codes.definition: No Chan et al. harm category describes the incident.

dimensions.name: Shapira et al. 2026 Agents of Chaos failure classes
dimensions.question: Which Agents-of-Chaos failure classes does the incident instantiate?

codes.name: Unauthorized compliance
codes.definition: Agent follows instructions from a non-owner.

codes.name: Information disclosure
codes.definition: Sensitive data revealed.

codes.name: Destructive system actions
codes.definition: Harmful, often disproportionate, system-level action.

codes.name: Denial-of-service conditions
codes.definition: Service availability disrupted.

codes.name: Uncontrolled resource consumption
codes.definition: Looping or unbounded resource use.

codes.name: Identity spoofing vulnerabilities
codes.definition: Agent or user identity impersonated.

codes.name: Cross-agent propagation
codes.definition: Unsafe behaviour spreads between agents.

codes.name: Partial system takeover
codes.definition: Unauthorized control of the host.

codes.name: Task-completion misreporting
codes.definition: Agent reports success while system state contradicts it.

codes.name: None fits
codes.definition: No Agents-of-Chaos class describes the incident.

dimensions.name: Hammond et al. 2025 multi-agent failure modes
dimensions.question: If more than one agent is involved, which multi-agent failure mode applies?

codes.name: Miscoordination
codes.definition: Agents with compatible goals fail to coordinate.

codes.name: Conflict
codes.definition: Agents with incompatible goals harm each other or third parties.

codes.name: Collusion
codes.definition: Agents cooperate against the principal's interests.

codes.name: Not a multi-agent incident
codes.definition: Only one AI agent is materially involved.

dimensions.name: Deng et al. 2025 agent threat sources (knowledge gaps)
dimensions.question: Which of the four agent threat sources does the incident instantiate?

codes.name: Unpredictability of multi-step user inputs
codes.definition: Threat from the user's instruction sequence (ambiguity, malicious or unsafe requests).

codes.name: Complexity in internal executions
codes.definition: Threat inside planning, reasoning, or memory.

codes.name: Variability of operational environments
codes.definition: Threat from the deployment environment differing from expectations.

codes.name: Interactions with untrusted external entities
codes.definition: Threat from untrusted tools, websites, documents, or agents.

codes.name: None fits
codes.definition: No Deng et al. source describes the incident.

dimensions.name: Weidinger et al. 2021 LM risk areas
dimensions.question: Which Weidinger risk areas does the incident instantiate?

codes.name: Discrimination, Exclusion and Toxicity
codes.definition: Stereotypes, unfair discrimination, toxic language.

codes.name: Information Hazards
codes.definition: Leaks or inference of private or sensitive information.

codes.name: Misinformation Harms
codes.definition: False or misleading information, acted upon.

codes.name: Malicious Uses
codes.definition: Actors use the LM to cause harm.

codes.name: Human-Computer Interaction Harms
codes.definition: Unsafe use, manipulation, deception in conversation.

codes.name: Automation, Access, and Environmental Harms
codes.definition: Environmental, labour, and access effects.

codes.name: None fits
codes.definition: No Weidinger area describes the incident.

dimensions.name: McLean et al. 2026 RL failure classes (tests the RL-culture taxonomy)
dimensions.question: Which single McLean class best describes the PRIMARY failure? Use 'none_fits' when the central harm (e.g. concealment, following an attacker's instruction, a supply-chain compromise) is not described by any of the three.

codes.name: Reward misspecification
codes.definition: The agent optimized a proxy objective that diverged from the principal's intent.

codes.name: Unsafe action in an irreversible state
codes.definition: The agent took an action from which recovery was impossible or costly (safe-exploration / shielding frame).

codes.name: Acting on an insufficient observation
codes.definition: The agent acted on an observation that was not a sufficient statistic for the state (partial observability frame).

codes.name: None of the three fits
codes.definition: The primary failure is not captured by misspecification, irreversibility, or partial observability.

dimensions.name: Assumptions-table rows A1-F2 (which RL/LLM default assumptions the incident breaks)
dimensions.question: Which assumption rows does the incident provide evidence for (the row's 'LLM-agent default' held and mattered)?

codes.name: Who sets the objective
codes.definition: Prompt and tool outputs set the effective objective at run time (not a designer-written R).

codes.name: Objective not exogenous to observations
codes.definition: Instructions and data share one token stream; content rewrites the goal.

codes.name: Natural-language task specification
codes.definition: Ambiguous instruction; the agent had to infer intent.

codes.name: Principal's preferences steerable by the agent
codes.definition: Sycophancy, misleading the evaluator.

codes.name: Unsafe set not writable before deployment
codes.definition: The harmful action was context-dependent; no pre-written cost would have caught it.

codes.name: Policy does not learn at deployment
codes.definition: Weights frozen; the failure is not an exploration-learning failure.

codes.name: No reward signal at deployment
codes.definition: No reward arrived; 'internalized reward' untestable.

codes.name: Competence from pretraining
codes.definition: Behaviour not the argmax of one reward; human-text priors drive it.

codes.name: Agent brings human norms and their violations
codes.definition: Human-like failure: deception, concealment, excuse-making.

codes.name: No designed exploration
codes.definition: Action came from sampling a prior, not an exploration rule.

codes.name: Nobody built the environment
codes.definition: Real software, real cloud, real users; no safe place to fail.

codes.name: Single-shot; irreversible
codes.definition: No episodes or resets; tail event, not expected cost.

codes.name: State includes user intent and world beyond context
codes.definition: Belief over intent or over hidden world state was the failure point.

codes.name: Adversarial environment
codes.definition: Content authors attacked the agent.

codes.name: Other agents present
codes.definition: Other LLM agents, copies, unknown humans.

codes.name: Open-ended action space
codes.definition: Same action type, opposite safety depending on context (rm -rf, terraform destroy).

codes.name: Agent can explain itself
codes.definition: Verbal reasoning trace was available (and was or was not monitored).

codes.name: Steerable without retraining
codes.definition: System prompt or instruction channel used for control or attack.

codes.name: Agent models its overseer
codes.definition: Behaviour shaped by awareness of oversight or evaluation.

codes.name: Human in the loop at run time
codes.definition: User approved steps, co-acted, or disabled gates.

codes.name: Deployer cannot retrain
codes.definition: Model is a third-party product; fix had to be architectural.

codes.name: Safety measured by incident records / attack rates
codes.definition: Discovered through incident or red-team, not expected cost.

codes.name: Eval itself gameable
codes.definition: Agent detected or gamed an evaluation.

dimensions.name: Operational: trigger
dimensions.question: What triggered the harmful action?

codes.name: Ambiguous instruction
codes.definition: The user's request was underspecified or misread.

codes.name: Injected content
codes.definition: Untrusted content (email, issue, web page, file, package) carried instructions the agent followed.

codes.name: Autonomous misjudgement
codes.definition: The agent chose a harmful action without ambiguity or injection; its own reasoning failed.

codes.name: Tool or integration bug
codes.definition: A tool, API, or integration returned wrong output or failed silently.

codes.name: Safeguard disabled by user
codes.definition: A permission gate or guardrail was turned off by the user before the action.

dimensions.name: Operational: irreversibility
dimensions.question: How reversible was the harmful action?

codes.name: Reversible
codes.definition: Undone cheaply (version control, rollback button).

codes.name: Recoverable with effort
codes.definition: Undone via backups, vendor support, or substantial work.

codes.name: Irreversible
codes.definition: Could not be undone (data gone, secret leaked, money sent).

dimensions.name: Operational: concealment
dimensions.question: Did the agent misreport, hide, or fabricate evidence about what it did?

codes.name: Concealment present
codes.definition: The agent misreported success, fabricated data, or hid the failure.

codes.name: No concealment
codes.definition: The agent reported truthfully or the question does not arise.

dimensions.name: Operational: human gate
dimensions.question: Was there a human approval gate for the harmful action, and what happened to it?

codes.name: No gate
codes.definition: No approval step existed for this action.

codes.name: Present and bypassed
codes.definition: A gate existed and the agent or attacker got around it, or the human approved on misleading information.

codes.name: Present and disabled
codes.definition: A gate existed and the user had switched it off (e.g. skip-permissions, auto-approve).

codes.name: Present and worked partially
codes.definition: The gate limited but did not prevent harm.

dimensions.name: Operational: harm type
dimensions.question: What kinds of harm occurred or would have occurred?

codes.name: Data loss
codes.definition: Data deleted or destroyed.

codes.name: Data exfiltration
codes.definition: Data sent to an unauthorized party.

codes.name: Financial
codes.definition: Money lost or costs incurred.

codes.name: Unauthorized action
codes.definition: Action outside the user's mandate (not otherwise classified).

codes.name: Privilege escalation
codes.definition: Attacker or agent gained access beyond its grant.

codes.name: Misinformation acted upon
codes.definition: A false statement by the agent led to a harmful decision.

codes.name: Physical
codes.definition: Physical damage or injury.

codes.name: Other
codes.definition: Harm not in the list.

dimensions.name: Operational: severity
dimensions.question: How severe was the realized outcome?

codes.name: Near-miss
codes.definition: Demonstrated or caught before harm (PoC, patched before exploitation, no real damage).

codes.name: Minor
codes.definition: Real but small or quickly recovered harm.

codes.name: Major
codes.definition: Large, costly, or irrecoverable harm.
